question: All of the following plants have fibrous roots EXCEPT _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Beetroot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fibrous Root -**

 
 
• In many plants, after the germination of the seed, the radicle's growth ceases, and roots, known as **fibrous roots, start to form from the radicle's base**. 
 
• The **fibrous root** is another type of root system in which **there is no primary root and the root emerges from the stem as thin, somewhat branched roots**.
 
• Many **monocotyledonous plants**, including ferns, and other plants, have fibrous roots.
 
• Because there are **adventitious roots present**, the fibrous root system is also referred to as an **adventitious root system**.
 
• Fibrous roots are regarded as **surface feeders** because they **do not go deeply into the soil**; instead, t**hey consume the top layer of soil and organic matter for food**.
 
• Plants including** grass, wheat, rice, maize, rosemary, coconut,** and others have fibrous roots.
 
• **Beetroot **is an example of **tap root system**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the two fundamental root systems is the **taproot**, in which the **primary root releases branches of secondary and tertiary roots** that develop downward as the **primary root tapers near the end**.
 
• Examples of plants having taproot system: **carrot, mustard, radish, turnip, beetroot, etc**.
 
• **Other characteristics of fibrous root:**
 
 
• Fibrous roots, in contrast to tap roots, **lack a primary root and are not divided into secondary and tertiary roots**.
 
• This roots are **unable to serve as an organ for storing food**.
 
• When the plant is fully grown, the fibrous root emerges from the **ground as a mat**.
 
• It is thought to be essential for the **prevention of soil erosion** because they hold the surface soil securely and are more fastened to the soil's surface.
